Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) tilts the assessment more negative. SLOOS indicates broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms for C&I loans (across firm sizes) and for CRE, as well as tighter standards on consumer credit (credit cards, autos, HELOCs, and many mortgage categories). Banks cited a weaker/uncertain economic outlook and reduced risk tolerance, reported weaker business loan demand on net, widespread forbearance/deferrals, and an expected deterioration in credit quality—pointing to further potential tightening ahead. These findings reinforce the statement’s emphasis on considerable downside risks, weak demand, and muted inflation pressures, and imply continued headwinds from the bank-lending channel despite improved market functioning. Partially offsetting, SLOOS shows strong demand for residential mortgages/refinancing amid lower rates, consistent with effective policy transmission via Treasury and agency MBS purchases. Net: moderately negative tone, tempered by credible policy support, but somewhat more negative than the FSR-only view.
